## QUESTION 1

__What was the earliest year that the name ‘Felisha’ was used?__

The earliest year that the name 'Felisha' was used was 1964.

```{python}
# Q1
import polars as pl

df = pl.read_csv('names_year_csv.csv')

# This code filters by name so that the table only shows the name we are looking for. It will also only show the name, year, and total so that we can easily see all relevant data. Finally it sorts the data by year so that the earliest year will appear at the top of the table.
df.filter(
  pl.col('name') == 'Felisha'
).select(
  pl.col('name'),pl.col('year'),pl.col('Total')
).sort(
  pl.col('year').abs(),descending=False
).head(1)
```


## QUESTION 2

__What year had the most babies named 'David'? How many babies were named 'David' that year?__

The year with the most babies born named David was 1955 with a total of 86,389.

```{python}
# Q2
import polars as pl

df = pl.read_csv('names_year_csv.csv')

# This code filters by name so that the table only shows the name we are looking for. It will also only show the name, year, and total so that we can easily see all relevant data. Finally it sorts the total so the highest number appaers at the top of the chart making it easiest to figure out the year.
df.filter(
  pl.col('name') == 'David'
).select(
  pl.col('name'),pl.col('year'),pl.col('Total')
).sort(
  pl.col('Total').abs(),descending=True
).head(1)
```


## QUESTION 3

__What year did your name hit its peak? How many babies were named your name in that year?__

My name hit its peak in both 1931 and 1933 with a total of 25 babies named Talmage in each of those two years.

```{python}
# Q3
import polars as pl

df = pl.read_csv('names_year_csv.csv')

# This code filters by my name so that the table only shows the name we are looking for. It will also only show the name, year, and total so that we can easily see all relevant data. Finally it sorts the total so the highest number appaers at the top of the chart making it easiest to figure out the year.
df.filter(
  pl.col('name') == 'Talmage'
).select(
  pl.col('name'),pl.col('year'),pl.col('Total')
).sort(
  pl.col('Total').abs(),descending=True
).head(2)
```


## QUESTION 4

__In the most recent year, what was the most common female name in Utah?__ 

The most common name genrally accepted as female in Utah in the most recent year with data was Olivia.

```{python}
# Q5
import polars as pl

df = pl.read_csv('names_year_csv.csv')

# This code filters by year so that the table only shows the most recent data from 2024. It will also only show the name, year, and total for Utah so that we can easily see all relevant data. Finally it sorts the total for Utah so the highest number appaers at the top of the chart making it easiest to figure out which Girl's name was the most popular that year.
df.filter(
  pl.col('year') == 2024
).select(
  pl.col('name'),
  pl.col('year'),
  pl.col('UT')
).sort(
  pl.col('UT').abs(),descending=True
).head(6)
```
